question: Refer to the exhibit. What is the result of executing this Python code?
context:
import time
import cli

date= time.strftime('%Y%m%d')
file= ('fusion-config_') + date
cli.execute ('copy running-config ftp://10.183.249.182/FusionSW/' + file)
exit()
options: It sends the switch configuration to Cisco TAC
It sends a Cisco device backup to a remote destination
It schedules a backup on a Cisco switch using EEM
It backs up Cisco switches to Cisco Prime Infrastructure
explanation: This will send a copy of the running configuration to an FTP server at 10.83.249.182.
theory: The script builds a dated filename with time.strftime() and then calls cli.execute('copy running-config ftp://.../filename') — this is the on-box Python interpreter directly issuing the NX-OS 'copy running-config' command to push a backup of the switch's configuration to a remote FTP server. Nothing here contacts Cisco TAC, schedules an EEM job, or integrates with Prime Infrastructure; it's simply a scripted remote configuration backup. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
